Love · Respect · Responsibility
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to our school!
Welcome to Yalding St Peter and St Paul Primary School, a small and welcoming Church of England village school where every child is known, valued and cared for.
With a maximum capacity of 168 pupils and a Published Admission Number (PAN) of 24, our size enables us to build strong relationships across our school community. We know our children as individuals and celebrate their unique strengths, interests, personalities and potential.
Our Christian vision, rooted in John 10:10, reminds us of our commitment to helping every child experience, 'life in all its fullness'.
We are proud to be a school where children can flourish, make meaningful relationships and develop the knowledge, skills and characters they need to make a positive difference in the world.

It is a pleasure to welcome you to our school community. This website is designed to keep families informed about school life and to offer new visitors a window into the work of our staff and governors, as well as the learning journey our children experience throughout their time with us.
We are very fortunate to have a dedicated, enthusiastic and caring team of staff and governors who work closely together to ensure that our school is a happy, safe and inspiring place to learn. Alongside our wider school community, we aim to create an environment where every child feels valued, respected and able to succeed.
As a Church of England school, our distinct Christian ethos is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our Christian values of love, respect and responsibility, we seek to create a nurturing environment where children are encouraged to care for one another, show compassion and take responsibility for their actions and learning. These values underpin daily life in our school and shape the way we learn, play and grow together as a community.
At the heart of our school is the belief that every child matters. We strive to provide high-quality teaching and learning experiences that meet the needs of all pupils, enabling them to grow in confidence, develop curiosity and become engaged learners. We encourage children to ask questions, think deeply and take pride in their achievements, all within a culture built on kindness, respect and responsibility. In line with our Christian ethos, we seek to offer children "life in all its fullness" (John 10:10), helping them to flourish academically, socially and spiritually.
We set high expectations for all pupils, both in their learning and in the way they treat others. We encourage children to do their very best in all they undertake, while also supporting them to develop strong personal values and positive attitudes. This helps to create a nurturing and purposeful environment where a love of learning can thrive.
We greatly value the partnership we have with parents and carers, recognising that children achieve their best when home and school work closely together. We encourage families to be actively involved in school life, as this shared commitment plays a vital role in supporting each child to reach their full potential.
We are proud of our school and the children who are part of it - children who are encouraged to grow into kind, responsible and thoughtful individuals. We look forward to working with you and welcoming you into our school community.

Remote Learning
Yalding St Peter and St Paul Church of England Primary School
At Yalding St Peter and St Paul Church of England Primary School, we are committed to ensuring that every child continues to receive a high-quality education should circumstances require the school, or part of the school, to close unexpectedly.
Our remote learning provision is designed to maintain pupils' learning, wellbeing and connection with their teachers while they are learning from home.
When Remote Learning Will Be Used
Remote learning may be implemented when:
The school is required to close due to exceptional circumstances, such as severe weather or loss of essential services.
A class or year group is unable to attend school.
Individual pupils are unable to attend school for an extended period, where appropriate.
Parents and carers will be informed as soon as possible through the school's usual communication channels.
How Will Remote Learning Work?
Whilst your child is learning from home, they will continue to receive learning that closely reflects the curriculum they would have been following in school. This helps to ensure that children continue to make good progress and do not miss important aspects of their education.
Learning for children in Years 1–6 will be printed, emailed or uploaded to Google Drive.
Children in the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) will have learning shared through Tapestry and parents are encouraged to upload photographs and observations of their child's learning for staff to celebrate and provide feedback.
Where appropriate, teachers may also send learning resources directly to families by email.
If you are unable to access online learning, please contact the school office. We will do our best to support families by:
helping you access our online learning platforms;
arranging the loan of a digital device where available; or
providing paper copies of learning where appropriate.
My Child Has Additional Needs. How Will Their Learning Work?
We recognise that some pupils, including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), may require additional support to access remote learning.
Where appropriate, we will:
provide personalised learning in line with your child's EHCP or individual support plan;
adapt learning activities to meet individual needs;
deliver learning through ClassDojo, Tapestry or directly to families where appropriate;
work closely with parents and carers to ensure pupils continue to make progress.
Daily Expectations
Children will receive approximately three hours of learning each day, in line with Department for Education guidance for primary-aged pupils.
Learning will normally include:
One wider curriculum (topic) activity
Practical, creative or physical activities where appropriate
Families are encouraged to:
complete the learning activities provided each day;
submit completed work where requested;
take regular breaks;
spend time being physically active.
We understand that every family's circumstances are different and will always work with parents where flexibility is needed.
Types of Learning
Learning activities may include:
recorded teaching videos;
teacher presentations and explanations;
worksheets prepared by teachers;
workbook activities;
educational websites;
practical investigations;
creative and project-based learning.
On the first day of an unexpected closure, we ask families to access the school's online learning platforms while teachers prepare and upload learning for the remainder of the closure.
If the school is closed due to snow, children may also receive a snow-day activity grid containing practical outdoor learning ideas where it is safe to do so.
Additional Learning Resources
Families may also wish to access:
Oak National Academy for teacher-led lessons across all year groups.
BBC Bitesize for engaging curriculum-based activities and revision.
These resources can be used alongside the learning provided by school.
Feedback and Support
Children should upload completed work to Google Drive where requested.
Teachers and teaching assistants will review submitted work and provide feedback during normal school hours where appropriate.
Feedback may include:
praise and encouragement;
recognition of successful learning;
suggestions for improvement;
next steps to support further learning.
Parents are encouraged to contact their child's class teacher if:
their child is finding learning difficult;
they require additional support;
they experience difficulties accessing online learning.
Safeguarding
The safety and wellbeing of our pupils remains our highest priority during any period of remote learning.
All online communication between staff, pupils and families will take place through approved school platforms and in accordance with the school's Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy and Online Safety Policy.
Children should always be supervised appropriately when accessing online learning.
Any safeguarding concerns should continue to be reported to the school immediately.
Working Together
Successful remote learning relies on a strong partnership between school and home.
We ask parents and carers to:
encourage children to engage positively with their learning;
help establish a suitable daily learning routine where possible;
supervise children when using online learning platforms;
communicate with the school if support is needed.
Our staff will:
provide appropriate learning activities that reflect the curriculum;
monitor engagement where possible;
provide feedback and guidance;
support pupils and families where required;
continue to promote children's wellbeing alongside their academic progress.
Thank you for your continued support.
By working together, we can ensure that every child at Yalding St Peter and St Paul Church of England Primary School continues to learn, achieve and flourish, whatever the circumstances.

Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS)
At Yalding Primary School, we are committed to providing every child with the very best start to their educational journey. Our Reception class follows the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework, which supports the learning, development and care of children from birth to five years old. The EYFS provides the foundations for lifelong learning, helping children to develop the skills, knowledge, confidence and resilience they need to thrive.
Our Reception Curriculum
We believe in educating the whole child, placing equal importance on intellectual, social, emotional, physical and creative development. We celebrate the unique qualities, experiences and cultural backgrounds that every child brings to our school community, ensuring that all children feel valued, respected and included. This reflects our school Christian values of Love, Respect and Responsibility, which are at the heart of everything we do.
Our carefully planned curriculum combines adult-led learning, child-initiated activities and purposeful play, creating a stimulating environment where children are encouraged to explore, question and discover. Learning experiences are designed to build independence, curiosity and confidence while supporting progress across all areas of the EYFS curriculum.
Learning Through Play
Play is central to learning in Reception. Through a wide range of engaging indoor and outdoor experiences, children have opportunities to investigate, create, problem-solve, collaborate and develop their communication skills. Play enables children to practise and consolidate new learning in meaningful and enjoyable ways, fostering a lifelong love of learning.
A Nurturing and Inspiring Environment
Every day in Reception is filled with exciting opportunities that encourage children to learn through exploration and discovery. Our nurturing environment supports children to take risks, develop positive relationships and become confident learners. By responding to children's interests and individual needs, we ensure that learning is both challenging and enjoyable.
At Yalding Primary School, we strive to create a caring and engaging learning environment where every child can flourish personally, socially, emotionally and academically, laying strong foundations for future success.

Our School Approach
At Yalding St Peter and St Paul Primary School, we are dedicated to creating a supportive and ambitious learning environment where every child is encouraged to succeed. We aim to nurture both academic progress and personal development, ensuring pupils are well-prepared for the next stage of their education.
To support this, we use a range of carefully planned strategies designed to stretch pupils while also addressing any barriers to learning. We are committed to ensuring that all pupils eligible for the pupil premium, regardless of their starting points, are supported to make strong and sustained progress.
When deciding how to allocate pupil premium funding, we make informed choices based on educational research. In particular, we refer to the Education Endowment Foundation and its Teaching and Learning Toolkit, which evaluates the impact and cost-effectiveness of different approaches.
Our provision includes:
consistently high-quality teaching across all classes
effective and targeted use of teaching assistants
mastery approaches to deepen understanding
one-to-one support where appropriate
encouraging strong partnerships with parents and carers
focused support for reading comprehension
small group teaching sessions
programmes that promote social and emotional wellbeing
Assessment and monitoring
On entry to the school, pupils are assessed to identify any early language or learning needs. This enables staff to put in place appropriate support and interventions from the outset, particularly in the early years.
We maintain a strong focus on tracking pupil progress and evaluating the impact of our provision. This includes the use of assessment data and regular pupil progress meetings involving both teaching and support staff.
Pupils who are not making expected progress are identified quickly and provided with additional support. Disadvantaged pupils are discussed at every progress meeting, including those who are currently meeting expectations, to ensure they continue to achieve well.
We regularly review our pupil premium provision to ensure it is effective and continues to meet the needs of all eligible pupils, including those who are higher attaining.
We recognise the importance of working closely with families. School staff engage with parents and carers to help overcome potential challenges outside of school and to support children’s learning and aspirations.

In 2026–2027, Chestnut Class is a Reception class, welcoming children who are all beginning their first year of school together. This is a change from the previous year, when the class was a mixed Reception and Year 1 provision. Having a dedicated Reception class will allow us to focus fully on the unique needs, interests and developmental stages of our youngest learners, providing a carefully planned curriculum and environment that supports children as they settle into school life, build confidence and develop the foundations for their future learning.

Staff followed the principles and commitments of the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS), which set out the standards for learning, development and care for all children in the Foundation Stage.

Religious Education
At Yalding Primary School, Religious Education is an important part of our Curriculum. Through the teaching of RE, we aim to develop children who are curious, thoughtful, respectful and able to reflect on the beliefs, values and experiences of others. RE provides children with opportunities to explore questions of meaning, purpose, identity and morality, helping them to develop their own understanding of the world and their place within it.
Our RE curriculum gives children the time and space to learn about Christianity and a range of other religions and worldviews. Through engaging lessons, stories, discussion, reflection and practical experiences, children develop their knowledge and understanding of different beliefs and traditions. They are encouraged to recognise both similarities and differences between faiths, fostering respect, empathy and an appreciation of diversity.
RE supports the development of the whole child by nurturing spiritual, moral, social and cultural development. Children are encouraged to ask thoughtful questions, consider different perspectives and reflect on how beliefs influence the way people live. Through exploring ethical and moral issues, pupils develop their ability to reason, make connections and form their own considered views, while understanding that others may hold different beliefs.
Our RE teaching is enriched through visits, visitors and opportunities to encounter religion as a lived experience. These experiences help children connect their classroom learning to the wider world and develop a deeper understanding of how faith shapes people’s lives.
Ultimately, RE at Yalding Primary School contributes to our vision of developing well-rounded, compassionate and reflective individuals. It enables children not only to learn about religion, but also to consider the lessons religions can offer, supporting them in becoming respectful members of our school, local and wider communities.
How is cultural capital developed through the RE curriculum?
At Yalding Primary School, cultural capital is developed through our RE curriculum by providing children with meaningful opportunities to explore different religions, cultures, beliefs and values. We work closely with the local parish and wider community to support the development of moral values and deepen children's understanding of the world around them.
Charitable links remain an important focus, encouraging children to develop compassion, generosity and a sense of responsibility towards others. RE also provides opportunities for children to experience awe and wonder, encouraging curiosity and reflection on the world in which they live.
What does impact look like in RE?
At Yalding Primary School, the impact of our RE curriculum is seen in children who develop a secure knowledge and understanding of the Christian faith and other religions and worldviews, while being encouraged to reflect on their own beliefs, values and faith journey.
Through confident and skilled teaching, alongside meaningful wider experiences, children enjoy their RE learning and make connections between their own lives, the life and teachings of Jesus and the experiences of people in their community and the wider world. They develop a broader understanding of their place in the world, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to understand themselves and others.
The impact of RE is evident in children who:
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding: Children can explain key beliefs, stories, practices and teachings within Christianity and other religions and worldviews, making links between beliefs and how people live.
Reflect and make connections: Children confidently relate RE learning to their own experiences, the life of Jesus and the lives of others, considering questions of meaning, purpose and morality.
Develop resilience and self-awareness: Children gain a wider perspective on their place in the world, helping them to understand themselves, navigate challenges and develop a strong sense of identity.
Show respect and appreciation: Children listen to and value the views of others, recognising and respecting differences in faith, belief and culture, including the perspectives of those with no faith or belief.
Demonstrate compassion and empathy: Children develop an understanding of the experiences of others and are encouraged to respond with kindness, compassion and consideration.
Develop strong moral values: Children use their learning to reflect on ethical and moral questions, applying Christian and Gospel values to their own choices and relationships.
Have high aspirations: Children approach their next steps with confidence, resilience and a growing awareness of their responsibilities to themselves, others and the wider world.
Ultimately, the impact of RE is reflected in children who are knowledgeable, reflective, respectful, compassionate and resilient, with the understanding and moral foundations to contribute positively to their school, community and wider society.
